lines.text: My grandfather grew roses in an old glass greenhouse behind his house.
When he went into the hospital, I stayed to keep them watered.
He left me one rule, written on a seed packet. If the glass fogs up at night... don't wipe it.
The first two nights, the greenhouse sat clear and dark under the moon.
On the third night, I saw it from the kitchen window. Every pane had gone white.
Not from the cold. It was fogging from the inside.
Then a small round patch cleared... and fogged again. Slow. Like breathing.
I walked out there with a flashlight. I told myself it was just the sprinklers.
Up close, I could hear it. A soft, wet breath against the glass... an inch from my face.
I pulled my sleeve over my hand... and wiped one pane clean.
There was nothing inside. Just the roses. Every single one, turned toward the house.
This morning, the greenhouse glass was perfectly clear.
But every window in my bedroom... is fogged from the inside.
